prompt: Some educators argue that computer coding should become a compulsory subject for all secondary school students, alongside mathematics and languages. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
partsToAddress: State clearly whether and to what extent you agree or disagree with making coding compulsory
Develop reasons supporting your position with specific explanations and consequences
Address the competing perspective on curriculum breadth and student diversity

ideaBank.idea: Early exposure to coding cultivates structured problem-solving habits applicable across disciplines.
ideaBank.develop: Breaking a complex task into logical steps trains pupils to debug errors systematically, a method that strengthens analytical writing and scientific enquiry alike.

ideaBank.idea: Compulsory instruction narrows socio-economic disparities in digital literacy.
ideaBank.develop: When coding is offered only as an after-school club, students from affluent households dominate enrolment, whereas universal classes ensure equal foundational access.

ideaBank.idea: Understanding how software operates prepares citizens to evaluate automated systems critically.
ideaBank.develop: Teenagers who grasp basic algorithms are less likely to accept biased online recommendations or opaque data collection practices uncritically.

ideaBank.idea: Mandating full programming courses risks crowding out arts, humanities, and physical education.
ideaBank.develop: Because timetable hours are finite, adding another examined core subject often forces schools to trim music, history, or studio art, undermining a well-rounded education.

ideaBank.idea: Many secondary schools lack qualified specialist teachers and up-to-date computing laboratories.
ideaBank.develop: In underfunded districts, compelling non-specialist staff to deliver technical syllabuses can produce dry, repetitive lessons that alienate learners from technology.

ideaBank.idea: Rapid advances in automated software generation may render specific coding languages obsolete.
ideaBank.develop: Spending years drilling syntax in one language offers limited long-term value compared with teaching broader mathematical reasoning and adaptable communication skills.

band8Model.text:
Debate over secondary school timetables increasingly centres on whether computer coding warrants the same mandatory status as mathematics and languages. While I agree that introductory computational thinking should be compulsory in the early secondary years, I contend that advanced programming ought to remain an elective rather than a universal requirement.

Integrating basic coding into the lower secondary curriculum delivers clear academic and civic benefits. Learning how to decompose a complex problem into logical sequences fosters analytical rigour that transfers readily to science, economics, and structured writing. Equally important is social equity: when technical instruction is restricted to optional clubs or fee-paying holiday workshops, pupils from lower-income families are disproportionately excluded from rapidly expanding career pathways. Requiring every twelve- to fourteen-year-old to complete foundational modules equips all adolescents with essential digital literacy, enabling them to scrutinise automated tools rather than merely consume them.

Nevertheless, elevating full software development to a compulsory examined subject throughout secondary schooling would prove counterproductive. School timetables are finite, and forcing reluctant learners to master intricate syntax inevitably narrows the curriculum at the expense of literature, visual arts, and practical vocational crafts. Moreover, specialist computing teachers remain scarce in many state systems; where schools in regional districts are obliged to staff mandatory courses without trained educators or reliable hardware, instruction quickly deteriorates into mechanical drills. Given that programming languages evolve swiftly, coercing students with strengths in nursing, carpentry, or music into prolonged technical training misallocates scarce instructional hours.

In conclusion, secondary systems should strike a calibrated balance. Making foundational coding compulsory during initial secondary years secures equitable digital competence, whereas keeping advanced programming optional thereafter preserves the breadth of a well-rounded education.

notes.noteVi: Mở bài nêu lập trường có sắc thái (đồng ý một phần có điều kiện) rõ ràng ngay câu luận điểm.
Dùng đảo ngữ với tính từ ở đầu mệnh đề kết hợp dấu hai chấm để nhấn mạnh luận điểm công bằng xã hội.
Cặp động từ đối lập chuẩn học thuật "scrutinise ... rather than merely consume" sắc nét, đúng chính tả Anh.
Câu chủ đề chuyển hướng lập luận mượt mà bằng "Nevertheless" và cụm danh động từ tóm gọn ý đối lập.
Kết hợp collocation "narrow the curriculum" với cụm "at the expense of" diễn đạt hệ quả đánh đổi chính xác.
Mệnh đề phân từ nguyên nhân ("Given that...") nối với chủ ngữ danh động từ dài mà vẫn giữ cấu trúc câu chặt chẽ.
Kết bài tổng hợp lại lập trường cân bằng một cách nhất quán mà không đưa thêm ý mới.

prompt: Governments should impose a substantial carbon tax on domestic flights to discourage short-distance air travel and fund cleaner rail networks. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
partsToAddress: Take a clear position on imposing a carbon tax on domestic aviation
Evaluate how the tax affects passenger choices and clean rail investment
Consider potential drawbacks such as regional isolation or equity for lower-income travellers

ideaBank.idea: Short-haul flights emit far more carbon per passenger-kilometre than electrified rail.
ideaBank.develop: Because aircraft burn a disproportionate share of fuel during take-off and climb, shifting journeys under five hundred kilometres onto trains curbs transport emissions rapidly.

ideaBank.idea: Pricing carbon corrects a market distortion that currently favours aviation over rail.
ideaBank.develop: Aviation fuel has long enjoyed tax exemptions in many jurisdictions, leaving budget airfares artificially cheaper than train tickets despite higher environmental costs.

ideaBank.idea: Hypothecated tax receipts can finance high-speed rail upgrades and lower ticket prices.
ideaBank.develop: Channelling aviation levies directly into track electrification and modern rolling stock creates a virtuous cycle that makes rail faster and more dependable.

ideaBank.idea: Remote island and mountainous communities often lack any viable rail alternative.
ideaBank.develop: Residents travelling from peripheral towns to regional hospitals or universities would face punitive travel bills without a feasible low-carbon substitute.

ideaBank.idea: Flat ticket levies disproportionately burden modest-income households.
ideaBank.develop: Whereas wealthy corporate travellers absorb higher fares easily, families visiting distant relatives might be priced out of occasional domestic trips.

ideaBank.idea: Sharply reduced domestic schedules could weaken regional tourism and business links.
ideaBank.develop: Smaller airports that rely on short commuter routes might lose commercial viability before rail corridors are completed, slowing local economic activity.

band8Model.text:
Short-distance aviation accounts for a disproportionately high share of transport emissions, as aircraft consume substantial fuel during take-off and ascent. I largely agree that governments should levy a significant carbon tax on domestic flights to curb avoidable air travel and finance cleaner rail services, provided that remote regions without viable alternatives are protected.

The strongest argument for taxing domestic aviation rests on both environmental pricing and public finance. In many nations, jet fuel remains lightly taxed compared with road petrol or rail electricity, creating a perverse market signal in which a one-hour flight costs less than an equivalent train journey. Imposing a meaningful carbon charge compels airlines and passengers to internalise these ecological costs, encouraging travellers on busy intercity corridors to switch to rail. Crucially, earmarking the revenue for rail modernisation ensures the policy does not merely penalise mobility; instead, it accelerates track electrification, expands seating capacity, and lowers off-peak train fares.

Critics rightly observe that a uniform levy risks penalising citizens in geographically isolated areas, such as archipelago communities or rural basins separated by mountain ranges, where rail construction is prohibitively expensive. Flat surcharges can also fall heavily on low-income households visiting family. Yet these concerns argue for thoughtful design rather than abandonment of the tax. Authorities can exempt essential lifeline routes lacking fast rail connections and structure the levy progressively so that frequent flyers and business-class cabins contribute the largest share, thereby mitigating social inequity without diluting the environmental incentive.

In summary, a well-calibrated carbon tax on domestic flights represents a practical fiscal lever for cutting aviation emissions and upgrading rail infrastructure. When accompanied by targeted exemptions for underserved regions, its environmental and economic gains clearly justify its adoption.

notes.noteVi: Lập trường đồng ý kèm điều kiện rõ ràng ngay cuối mở bài, trả lời trực tiếp cả hai vế của đề.
Cụm từ kinh tế học chính xác ("perverse market signal", "internalise these ecological costs") nâng điểm Lexical Resource.
Liên kết ý nhân quả chặt chẽ giữa hai vế tương phản bằng dấu chấm phẩy và "instead", kèm cấu trúc song song ba động từ.
Mệnh đề quan hệ không xác định với "where" kết hợp cụm phân từ quá khứ "separated by..." thể hiện cấu trúc câu đa dạng.
Câu bản lề ngắn gọn phản biện lập luận trái chiều và nối tự nhiên sang phần giải pháp thiết kế chính sách.
Dùng "thereby + V-ing" cùng cặp động từ học thuật "mitigating ... without diluting" rất tự nhiên.
Mệnh đề trạng ngữ rút gọn ("When accompanied by...") giúp câu kết cô đọng và học thuật.

prompt: Secondary schools should enforce a complete ban on personal smartphones during classroom lessons. Do you agree or disagree with this view?
partsToAddress: Express a clear stance on banning personal smartphones during lessons
Explain how smartphone presence or absence affects focus, behaviour, and academic results
Address arguments for educational use or parent-student communication

ideaBank.idea: Even silent notifications fragment teenage concentration during demanding lessons.
ideaBank.develop: Glancing repeatedly at incoming messages forces learners to reset their working memory, reducing comprehension of complex explanations in mathematics or literature.

ideaBank.idea: Removing personal devices helps maintain classroom discipline and curbs covert bullying.
ideaBank.develop: Without phones on desks, pupils are far less able to record classmates or teachers without consent and share embarrassing clips online.

ideaBank.idea: A uniform ban reduces peer pressure linked to owning expensive handset models.
ideaBank.develop: Students from modest backgrounds are spared daily status comparisons when every device remains locked away until the end of lessons.

ideaBank.idea: Smartphones can act as convenient research and polling tools during interactive lessons.
ideaBank.develop: Teachers in schools with limited tablet budgets sometimes use mobile quizzes or language dictionaries to check understanding rapidly.

ideaBank.idea: Outright prohibition may miss an opportunity to teach adolescents responsible self-regulation.
ideaBank.develop: Opponents contend that young people eventually enter universities and workplaces where they must manage constant notifications independently.

ideaBank.idea: Some parents prefer direct contact with their children for safety or logistical changes.
ideaBank.develop: Families juggling shifting work hours argue that quick text updates about after-school collection provide practical reassurance.

band8Model.text:
Personal smartphones have become ubiquitous among adolescents, prompting intense debate over their place in secondary classrooms. I firmly agree that schools should enforce a complete ban on personal handsets during lessons, as their presence undermines sustained concentration and classroom order while offering no educational benefit that dedicated school equipment cannot deliver better.

The primary justification for prohibition lies in the cognitive cost of constant distraction. Even when switched to silent mode, a phone resting on a desk competes for a teenager's attention through vibrating alerts and the habit of checking social feeds. Interruptions lasting only seconds disrupt working memory, making it markedly harder for pupils to follow multi-step proofs or sustained textual analysis. Equally concerning is the social friction phones introduce: covert filming of classmates or staff erodes mutual trust and complicates teachers' efforts to maintain discipline. Removing devices to secure lockers at the start of lessons restores a calm, focused environment that supports stronger educational outcomes, particularly for students who already struggle with study habits.

Admittedly, opponents argue that allowing phones teaches young people self-regulation and provides convenient access to dictionaries or interactive quizzes. Yet expecting adolescents to resist applications engineered specifically to capture attention is unrealistic during high-stakes instructional time; self-management is more sensibly practised outside lesson hours. Similarly, digital tasks are far better supported by school-owned tablets or laptops that restrict off-task platforms and guarantee identical hardware for every learner. As for urgent family messages, school reception desks have reliably handled emergency contact for decades.

In conclusion, banning personal smartphones during classroom lessons is a proportionate and evidence-backed measure. Far from rejecting digital literacy, it protects the deep attention that meaningful learning requires while leaving technology use to purposeful, school-managed tools.

notes.noteVi: Quan điểm đồng ý hoàn toàn được nêu dứt khoát kèm tóm tắt hai trụ cột lập luận chính.
Câu chủ đề định hướng rõ trọng tâm đoạn thân bài 1 (chi phí nhận thức của sự xao nhãng) mà không dùng từ nối máy móc.
Collocation tự nhiên ("erodes mutual trust", "maintain discipline") cùng từ vựng chính xác "covert filming".
Dùng "Admittedly" để nhượng bộ có kiểm soát trước khi phản bác từng ý bằng "Yet" và "Similarly".
Chủ ngữ danh động từ kết hợp mệnh đề phân từ bị động rút gọn ("engineered specifically to...") gọn gàng, chính xác.
Cấu trúc "Far from + V-ing" ở kết bài giúp bác bỏ hiểu lầm phổ biến một cách thanh lịch.
Cụm tính từ ghép học thuật chuẩn xác ("proportionate", "evidence-backed") nâng chất lượng từ vựng kết bài.

prompt: Imposing a government levy on sugar-sweetened soft drinks is the most effective way to reduce diet-related illness in the population. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
partsToAddress: Evaluate the claim that a sugar levy is the SINGLE most effective policy
Explain how a beverage tax works on both manufacturers and consumers
Compare the levy with complementary public health strategies

ideaBank.idea: Tiered sugar levies prompt beverage companies to reformulate recipes swiftly.
ideaBank.develop: When higher sugar thresholds attract steeper tax bands, producers lower sucrose content across entire product lines to protect retail margins, cutting population intake automatically.

ideaBank.idea: Higher retail prices discourage impulsive purchases among price-sensitive youths.
ideaBank.develop: Teenagers with limited pocket money are especially responsive to price increases at corner shops and vending machines, reducing habitual consumption of sugary sodas.

ideaBank.idea: Revenue collected from the levy can fund preventive health and school sports.
ideaBank.develop: Allocating tax proceeds to school kitchens and community exercise facilities multiplies the policy's protective effect on childhood obesity.

ideaBank.idea: Liquid sugar represents only one component of an unhealthy modern diet.
ideaBank.develop: Consumers who cut back on carbonated drinks may still ingest excessive calories and refined carbohydrates from ultra-processed snacks, confectionery, and fast food.

ideaBank.idea: Taxation alone does not improve access to affordable fresh produce.
ideaBank.develop: In low-income neighbourhoods where fresh fruit and vegetables remain costly or scarce, penalising soft drinks without subsidising nutritious food yields modest health gains.

ideaBank.idea: Lasting dietary change requires nutrition education and stricter marketing curbs.
ideaBank.develop: Clear front-of-pack warning labels and bans on junk-food advertising aimed at children reshape lifelong eating habits more deeply than a single product tax.

band8Model.text:
Rising rates of type two diabetes and dental decay have prompted many governments to introduce fiscal levies on sugar-sweetened beverages. While I agree that such taxation is a proven tool for curbing sugar intake, I disagree that it is the single most effective means of reducing diet-related illness across an entire population.

A tiered sugar levy certainly delivers rapid, measurable benefits that voluntary industry pledges rarely achieve. By taxing drinks more heavily above specific gram-per-litre thresholds, authorities give manufacturers a compelling commercial motive to reformulate recipes rather than pass higher prices onto shoppers. Consequently, total sugar consumption drops even among consumers who never alter their purchasing habits. At the same time, noticeable price increases deter habitual purchases among price-sensitive adolescents, while the resulting revenue can be directed towards preventive healthcare and school meal upgrades.

Nevertheless, treating a beverage tax as the paramount solution overlooks the wider nutritional environment driving chronic disease. Soft drinks account for only a fraction of excess calorie intake; ultra-processed snacks, ready meals, and sugary baked goods contribute heavily to obesity yet remain untouched by a narrow drinks levy. Furthermore, taxation merely penalises unhealthy choices without removing the barriers to balanced eating. If fresh vegetables, lean proteins, and clean drinking water remain expensive or inconvenient in deprived districts, families will simply substitute untaxed sweet snacks. Enduring reductions in diet-related illness therefore depend on a comprehensive package combining clear front-of-pack labelling, restrictions on junk-food advertising to minors, subsidies for fresh produce, and practical nutrition education.

In conclusion, a sugar levy on soft drinks is a valuable catalyst for reformulation and reduced consumption, but it is far from sufficient on its own. Safeguarding public health most effectively requires embedding fiscal measures within broader food-system reforms.

notes.noteVi: Xử lý chính xác từ khóa so sánh nhất "the most effective" trong đề bài bằng lập trường phản biện sắc bén.
Từ vựng chính sách công và dinh dưỡng chính xác ("tiered sugar levy", "gram-per-litre thresholds", "reformulate recipes").
Liên từ hệ quả "Consequently" nối trực tiếp cơ chế cải tiến công thức của hãng với tác động ở cấp độ dân số.
Chuyển sang thân bài 2 bằng lập luận trực diện vào giới hạn phạm vi của thuế đồ uống có đường.
Câu điều kiện loại 1 kết hợp cụm danh từ đồng đẳng rõ ràng để minh họa hiệu ứng thay thế ngoài ý muốn.
Cụm danh từ mở rộng bằng phân từ hiện tại ("combining...") liệt kê bốn giải pháp song song mạch lạc.
Sử dụng collocation "safeguard public health" kết hợp động từ "embedding ... within" tự nhiên và chuẩn Band 8.

prompt: Municipal authorities should permanently ban private cars from historic city centres, even if this causes inconvenience for local commuters and businesses. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
partsToAddress: State clearly your stance on permanently banning private vehicles from historic cores
Discuss environmental, heritage, and liveability benefits of pedestrianisation
Weigh the short-term inconvenience to commuters and merchants and how it can be managed

ideaBank.idea: Narrow medieval or colonial street grids were never engineered for private motor traffic.
ideaBank.develop: Removing cars eliminates severe bottlenecks and protects fragile stone facades from exhaust particulates and heavy vibration.

ideaBank.idea: Pedestrianised centres significantly improve local air quality and street safety.
ideaBank.develop: Lower nitrogen dioxide and noise levels transform central squares into welcoming civic spaces for children, older residents, and outdoor dining.

ideaBank.idea: Retail footfall frequently increases once streets become pleasant to walk along.
ideaBank.develop: Although shopkeepers initially fear losing motorists, calmer streets encourage pedestrians to linger, browse independent stores, and spend more at cafes.

ideaBank.idea: Suburban commuters face longer journeys when direct driving access is removed.
ideaBank.develop: Without park-and-ride hubs and frequent buses on the perimeter, workers from outer suburbs experience frustrating transfers and lost productivity.

ideaBank.idea: Small merchants rely on dependable van access for stock deliveries and waste collection.
ideaBank.develop: Strict blanket restrictions can raise logistics costs for independent grocers and restaurants if off-peak freight windows are poorly planned.

ideaBank.idea: Older residents and people with mobility impairments may become isolated.
ideaBank.develop: Elderly citizens living in central flats who cannot walk long distances to tram stops need exemptions for electric shuttles or blue-badge vehicles.

band8Model.text:
Historic city centres were laid out centuries before the private automobile, yet many remain choked by congested lanes and kerbside parking. I strongly agree that municipal authorities should permanently exclude private cars from these districts, as the long-term gains in air quality, heritage preservation, and commercial vitality far outweigh the transitional inconvenience.

Reclaiming central streets from motor traffic directly safeguards both human health and irreplaceable architecture. Vehicle exhaust accelerates the chemical erosion of historic stonework while exposing pedestrians to hazardous fine particulates and persistent noise pollution. Once private cars are removed, councils can allocate urban space to shaded walkways, cycle lanes, and public seating, turning cramped thoroughfares into thriving civic hubs. Contrary to the common fear that banning motorists devastates local trade, pedestrianised quarters often enjoy stronger retail turnover because visitors move at a slower pace and spend more readily in independent shops and street-side cafes.

The objections raised by suburban commuters and shopkeepers deserve practical mitigation rather than capitulation. An abrupt ban imposed without alternative mobility options would understandably frustrate workers from outlying towns and complicate stock deliveries. However, well-planned cities resolve these bottlenecks by constructing peripheral park-and-ride facilities, expanding frequent electric bus loops, and permitting commercial vans to enter during early-morning windows. Equally vital are targeted permits for residents with mobility impairments and emergency vehicles, ensuring that a car-free core remains genuinely accessible to every citizen rather than only the able-bodied.

In conclusion, preserving private car access in narrow historic quarters sacrifices public health and architectural heritage for an inefficient mode of urban travel. Provided councils pair permanent restrictions with reliable public transport and sensible logistics exemptions, car-free centres offer a demonstrably superior model for contemporary cities.

notes.noteVi: Khẳng định lập trường dứt khoát và cân nhắc trực tiếp yếu tố "inconvenience" được nêu trong đề bài.
Từ vựng chuyên sâu về đô thị và môi trường ("chemical erosion", "fine particulates", "noise pollution") rất chính xác.
Dùng cụm tương phản "Contrary to..." để lật lại giả định phổ biến về tác hại kinh doanh một cách thuyết phục.
Cặp danh từ trừu tượng đối lập "practical mitigation rather than capitulation" nâng sắc thái nghị luận lên Band 8+.
Đảo ngữ ("Equally vital are...") kết hợp mệnh đề phân từ hệ quả ("ensuring that...") đa dạng hóa cấu trúc ngữ pháp.
Mệnh đề điều kiện trang trọng với "Provided..." giúp kết bài chặt chẽ và có chiều sâu thực tiễn.
Triển khai cụ thể hóa collocation "allocate urban space" bằng ba ví dụ trực quan, giúp đoạn văn có sức thuyết phục.

prompt: Employers should transition to a standard four-day working week with no reduction in pay, as shorter hours lead to happier and more productive staff. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
partsToAddress: State to what extent you agree with adopting a four-day week on full pay
Examine how reduced hours affect employee wellbeing, focus, and productivity
Evaluate sectoral constraints where shorter weeks raise staffing or cost pressures

ideaBank.idea: Rested employees concentrate more deeply and waste less time on low-value tasks.
ideaBank.develop: Knowing that weekly output must fit into four days encourages teams to trim redundant meetings and protect uninterrupted blocks for complex problem-solving.

ideaBank.idea: An extra weekday off markedly lowers burnout and costly staff turnover.
ideaBank.develop: Workers can handle medical appointments, caregiving, and rest without exhausting annual leave, reducing absenteeism and recruitment expenses for employers.

ideaBank.idea: Shorter commuting schedules yield secondary environmental and household savings.
ideaBank.develop: Cutting one weekday of office travel trims transport emissions and lowers weekly childcare or commuting outlays for working families.

ideaBank.idea: Frontline services requiring continuous staffing cannot simply compress hours without hiring more people.
ideaBank.develop: Hospital wards, primary schools, and care homes depend on physical presence across fixed shifts, meaning a four-day standard on full pay would inflate wage bills sharply.

ideaBank.idea: Small businesses with tight profit margins may struggle to maintain client coverage.
ideaBank.develop: A five-person engineering workshop or local pharmacy cannot easily stagger rotas without delaying orders or losing customers to seven-day competitors.

ideaBank.idea: Compressing five days of workload into four can inadvertently intensify daily stress.
ideaBank.develop: Where managers fail to redesign workflows, employees end up working ten-hour stretches that impair cognitive accuracy and strain family evenings.

band8Model.text:
Growing concern over workplace burnout has led numerous companies to trial a four-day working week while maintaining full salaries. Although I agree that shorter weeks can substantially enhance wellbeing and output in many office-based industries, I disagree that employers across every sector should adopt this model as a universal standard.

In knowledge-intensive fields such as software design, publishing, and financial analysis, productivity is governed by mental sharpness rather than hours spent at a desk. When staff receive a guaranteed third day of rest without financial penalty, work-related stress falls and voluntary resignations decline, saving firms substantial recruitment costs. Moreover, the constraint of a four-day schedule often prompts beneficial organisational discipline: managers eliminate unnecessary meetings, clarify priorities, and automate repetitive reporting so that teams deliver comparable output in fewer hours. Employees also gain time for family care and personal errands, fostering higher morale and sustained engagement.

Applying a one-size-fits-all approach across the wider economy, however, encounters rigid operational limits. Essential services such as emergency wards, public transport, and primary schools cannot compress human presence into thirty-two hours without either reducing service hours or hiring roughly twenty per cent more staff—an expense many public budgets and thin-margin small firms cannot absorb. Even in commercial offices, poorly managed transitions risk backfiring: if workloads remain untouched, employees simply endure exhausting ten-hour shifts that erode the very wellbeing the reform sought to protect.

In conclusion, a full-pay four-day week is a compelling innovation for sectors where output can be decoupled from attendance through smarter workflows. Rather than mandating it universally, policymakers and business leaders should encourage flexible trials alongside alternative arrangements, such as staggered shifts or hybrid schedules, suited to each industry's realities.

notes.noteVi: Lập trường phân hóa rõ theo ngành nghề ngay mở bài, thể hiện tư duy sắc sảo thay vì đồng ý/phản đối cực đoan.
Diễn đạt tự nhiên, chính xác về bản chất năng suất lao động trí óc ("governed by mental sharpness").
Dùng dấu hai chấm mở ra ba ví dụ cụ thể giải thích trực tiếp cơ chế tăng hiệu suất.
Đặt "however" ở giữa câu chủ đề thân bài 2 tạo nhịp chuyển mượt và tự nhiên hơn đặt ở đầu câu.
Cấu trúc "without either V-ing or V-ing" chính xác, diễn tả rõ thế lưỡng nan chi phí nhân sự.
Mệnh đề quan hệ rút gọn kép ("the very wellbeing [that] the reform sought to protect") rất tinh tế.
Cụm động từ học thuật "decoupled from" diễn đạt ngắn gọn cốt lõi điều kiện thành công của tuần làm việc 4 ngày.

prompt: As advertising revenue declines across traditional newspapers, governments should provide direct public funding to sustain independent journalism. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
partsToAddress: Take a clear stance on state financial support for independent news organisations
Explain why the collapse of commercial journalism threatens civic accountability
Address the risk of political interference and how editorial independence can be protected

ideaBank.idea: Investigative reporting performs a public-interest audit that commercial markets now underfund.
ideaBank.develop: Long-term scrutiny of municipal contracts, courts, and environmental breaches requires months of salaried reporting that click-driven online advertising rarely covers.

ideaBank.idea: Sustaining credible local newsrooms helps combat rampant online misinformation.
ideaBank.develop: When regional papers shut down, residents turn to unverified social media groups, leaving communities more susceptible to rumours and polarising falsehoods.

ideaBank.idea: Arm's-length trusts can disburse subsidies without compromising editorial autonomy.
ideaBank.develop: Independent boards allocating grants on transparent circulation or reporting criteria—or citizen voucher schemes—separate funding decisions from cabinet ministers.

ideaBank.idea: Financial dependence on the state creates a structural risk of subtle self-censorship.
ideaBank.develop: Editors aware that next year's budget rests with ruling politicians may soften critical coverage of government scandals to avoid funding cuts.

ideaBank.idea: Direct subsidies may undermine public trust by making outlets appear partisan.
ideaBank.develop: Even if newsrooms remain impartial, sceptical readers may dismiss state-backed reporting as official propaganda, weakening journalism's credibility.

ideaBank.idea: Taxpayer funds could prop up inefficient legacy papers unable to adapt to digital habits.
ideaBank.develop: Channeling public money to declining print operations may distort competition and crowd out agile subscriber-funded or non-profit digital start-ups.

band8Model.text:
The migration of advertising budgets to global technology platforms has hollowed out traditional newspapers, leaving many towns without professional reporters. I agree that governments should provide public funding to sustain independent journalism, but only if subsidies are channelled through strict arm's-length mechanisms that insulate newsrooms from political pressure.

The case for public intervention rests on the reality that rigorous reporting is a public good whose civic value exceeds its commercial profitability. Uncovering procurement fraud, tracking local court proceedings, or verifying public health claims demands trained journalists and months of patient enquiry—expenses that short-attention online advertising can no longer support. Where regional newspapers fold, civic oversight weakens and communities become far more vulnerable to rampant misinformation circulating unchecked on social networks. Just as societies finance public libraries and universities because markets alone underprovide knowledge, modest public investment in news reporting safeguards informed democratic participation.

Nevertheless, direct grants administered by government ministries carry an undeniable danger: financial dependency can invite undue influence or quiet self-censorship. Should editors fear that probing a minister's policy might jeopardise next year's subsidy, the core purpose of a free press would be defeated, and public trust would quickly erode. Avoiding this pitfall requires institutional safeguards rather than laissez-faire neglect. Funding can be distributed by an autonomous statutory council governed by multi-year budgets, or via taxpayer journalism vouchers that let individual citizens direct public support to accredited outlets of their choice, thereby keeping politicians entirely removed from editorial selection.

In conclusion, allowing independent journalism to wither under digital market failure poses a serious risk to democratic accountability. Public funding is therefore warranted, provided it operates within a robust, depoliticised framework that protects editorial freedom above all else.

notes.noteVi: Lập trường đồng ý có điều kiện rất sắc nét, nêu ngay giải pháp thể chế ("arm's-length mechanisms") để giữ độc lập báo chí.
Dùng thuật ngữ kinh tế công ("public good", "commercial profitability") cực kỳ trúng chủ đề và học thuật.

Collocation "a robust framework" kết hợp tính từ học thuật "depoliticised" khép lại bài viết chặt chẽ.

prompt: Cities should abolish fares on municipal bus networks and finance the service entirely through local taxation. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
partsToAddress: State clearly whether you agree or disagree with making municipal buses completely free
Assess the social and mobility advantages of abolishing bus fares
Evaluate fiscal trade-offs and whether free fares actually reduce car congestion

ideaBank.idea: Zero-fare buses immediately relieve living costs for low-income commuters and students.
ideaBank.develop: Workers on minimum wages spend a sizeable fraction of disposable income on daily travel, so free transit widens access to jobs, clinics, and evening classes.

ideaBank.idea: Eliminating ticket inspection speeds up boarding and cuts administrative overheads.
ideaBank.develop: Passengers can board through all doors simultaneously, trimming dwell times at busy stops while freeing councils from maintaining costly ticketing hardware.

ideaBank.idea: Universal free transit removes stigma and simplifies daily mobility across the city.
ideaBank.develop: Tourists, casual riders, and elderly residents no longer navigate confusing zone tariffs, encouraging spontaneous off-peak trips that support local high streets.

ideaBank.idea: Abolishing fares rarely persuades committed motorists to abandon private cars.
ideaBank.develop: Car owners prioritise speed, punctuality, and route frequency over a modest bus fare, so free services mostly attract people who previously walked or cycled.

ideaBank.idea: Losing farebox revenue can starve municipal operators of funds needed to upgrade fleets.
ideaBank.develop: When local budgets tighten, a fully tax-funded network faces political pressure to cut routes or delay electric bus purchases, degrading service quality.

ideaBank.idea: Targeted fare concessions achieve equity at a much lower fiscal cost.
ideaBank.develop: Offering free passes to pensioners, students, and low-income earners while charging affluent commuters preserves capital for dedicated bus lanes and higher frequency.

band8Model.text:
Several municipalities have experimented with abolishing bus fares in an effort to curb congestion and broaden mobility. While I recognise the social appeal of zero-fare transit, I largely disagree with funding municipal buses entirely through local taxation, because service reliability—not ticket price—is the decisive barrier keeping drivers off public transport.

Proponents rightly highlight the immediate relief free buses bring to financially stretched households. For shift workers and students, daily fares consume a meaningful share of weekly income, and removing them guarantees equitable access to employment and healthcare. Abolishing ticket collection also allows all-door boarding, which trims stop delays and eliminates the expense of maintaining card readers and enforcement staff. In compact towns with light ridership, these administrative savings can offset a noticeable portion of lost ticket revenue.

In larger cities, however, eliminating fares across the board often fails to achieve its primary environmental goal. Most private motorists avoid buses not because a single ticket is unaffordable, but because infrequent schedules, indirect routes, and peak-hour congestion make journeys unpredictable. Consequently, zero-fare schemes tend to divert pedestrians and cyclists onto buses while leaving commuter car traffic largely intact. Worse still, surrendering farebox revenue places heavy strain on municipal tax revenue; during economic downturns, councils may be forced to postpone fleet electrification, trim evening services, or freeze route expansion. Investing public funds instead in dedicated bus lanes, real-time timetable displays, and targeted free passes for low-income citizens, students, and pensioners delivers far greater social and environmental returns.

In conclusion, although free municipal buses carry clear symbolic and equitable value, universal abolition of fares misallocates scarce transport budgets. Cities achieve cleaner streets and fairer mobility more effectively by pairing targeted fare concessions with sustained investment in fast, dependable networks.

notes.noteVi: Nêu rõ lập trường phản đối phần lớn và chỉ thẳng nguyên nhân cốt lõi (độ tin cậy dịch vụ quan trọng hơn giá vé).

Từ vựng giao thông đô thị chuẩn xác ("zero-fare schemes", "divert ... onto", "largely intact").
Dùng "Worse still" nâng cấp lập luận từ kém hiệu quả sang rủi ro tài khóa, giữ mạch logic leo thang chặt chẽ.
Chủ ngữ danh động từ mở rộng ("Investing public funds instead in...") đi kèm động từ số ít "delivers" chuẩn xác.
