prompt: Introducing an annual wealth tax on high-value luxury properties is a fair and practical method for narrowing economic inequality. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
partsToAddress: Evaluate both the fairness and the practicality of taxing high-value luxury properties
Analyse how property-based wealth taxation affects housing markets and public revenue
Address potential objections regarding liquidity, valuation, and investment deterrence

ideaBank.idea: Real estate is immobile and visible, making it far harder to shelter offshore than financial capital.
ideaBank.develop: Unlike shares or digital assets that can be shifted across jurisdictions overnight, luxury mansions and penthouses remain tied to land registries, ensuring high compliance.

ideaBank.idea: Taxing unearned capital gains in prime real estate promotes fiscal fairness.
ideaBank.develop: Luxury home values frequently surge due to public infrastructure and neighbourhood amenities rather than owner effort, so capturing a modest annual share is equitable.

ideaBank.idea: Levies on ultra-high-value dwellings cool speculative demand and fund affordable housing.
ideaBank.develop: Discouraging investors from hoarding vacant luxury units eases upward pressure on urban land prices while generating steady revenue for social housing construction.

ideaBank.idea: Asset-rich, cash-poor owners such as retirees may face liquidity hardship.
ideaBank.develop: Long-standing residents whose modest homes appreciated steeply over decades might lack the disposable income to pay recurring annual bills based on current market value.

ideaBank.idea: Regular, accurate valuation of unique luxury properties creates administrative friction.
ideaBank.develop: Bespoke estates sell infrequently, inviting costly legal disputes and appeals over official assessments that absorb part of the tax yield.

ideaBank.idea: Excessive property levies could deter residential construction and foreign capital.
ideaBank.develop: If set too steeply, recurring charges might reduce high-end redevelopment projects that employ skilled tradespeople and contribute stamp duties.

band8Model.text:
Widening gaps between wage earners and property owners have revived interest in taxing accumulated wealth rather than relying predominantly on income and consumption levies. I largely agree that an annual wealth tax on high-value luxury properties is both fair and practical for narrowing economic inequality, provided sensible liquidity safeguards are built into its design.

From an administrative perspective, luxury real estate overcomes the flaw that has undermined broader wealth taxes: capital flight. Financial portfolios can be restructured across offshore jurisdictions with relative ease, whereas penthouses and landed estates are physically immobile and recorded on public title deeds. Consequently, a progressive annual charge on properties exceeding a high threshold is difficult to evade and yields predictable fiscal revenue. It is equally defensible on grounds of fairness. Much of the appreciation in prime urban housing stems from publicly funded transport, parks, and zoning scarcity rather than productive enterprise; channelling a fraction of those unearned windfalls into affordable housing and state schools directly counteracts intergenerational wealth concentration while discouraging speculative hoarding of vacant luxury units.

Critics nonetheless highlight legitimate practical obstacles. Keeping valuations current for unique high-end homes can trigger costly appeals, and steep rates risk deterring residential investment if calibrated poorly. A more sympathetic concern involves retired homeowners whose family residences have risen sharply in price despite modest pension incomes. Yet modern fiscal policy can resolve these tensions straightforwardly: automated land-registry bands reduce valuation disputes, while deferral clauses allow cash-constrained retirees to settle accrued charges upon the eventual sale or inheritance of the estate rather than forcing premature relocation.

In conclusion, taxing luxury property combines high enforceability with strong redistributive logic. When paired with transparent thresholds and deferral options for older residents, it offers an equitable and workable tool for moderating extreme wealth disparities.

notes.noteVi: Trả lời trực diện cả hai tiêu chí "fair" và "practical" của đề bài, đồng thời đặt điều kiện thanh khoản rất thực tế.
Định khung góc nhìn hành chính ngay đầu đoạn và dùng dấu hai chấm tạo điểm nhấn thuyết phục cho cụm "capital flight".
Từ vựng kinh tế - pháp lý chính xác ("offshore jurisdictions", "landed estates", "public title deeds", "unearned windfalls").
Cụm danh động từ làm chủ ngữ đi kèm hai động từ tác động ("counteracts ... while discouraging") mượt mà, chặt chẽ.
Mệnh đề quan hệ sở hữu "whose..." kết hợp cụm nhượng bộ "despite..." diễn tả sắc thái đối tượng bị ảnh hưởng chính xác.
Thuật ngữ tài khóa nâng cao ("deferral clauses", "cash-constrained", "accrued charges") thể hiện vốn từ Band 8–9.
Kết bài tổng kết gọn hai tiêu chí "practical" (enforceability) và "fair" (redistributive logic) theo đúng yêu cầu đề.

prompt: Voting in national elections should be legally compulsory for all eligible citizens, with modest fines imposed on those who fail to participate. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
partsToAddress: Present a clear view on legally mandating voter turnout with modest fines
Analyse how compulsory voting affects representation, policy priorities, and legitimacy
Examine civil-liberty concerns and the risk of uninformed ballot casting

ideaBank.idea: Universal turnout ensures governments serve the whole electorate rather than only vocal blocs.
ideaBank.develop: When voting is voluntary, younger and lower-income citizens turn out at lower rates, prompting parties to tailor policies disproportionately towards wealthier older voters.

ideaBank.idea: Compulsory participation dampens political polarisation by rewarding centrist persuasion.
ideaBank.develop: Rather than spending vast sums mobilising extreme partisan bases, candidates must appeal to moderate, undecided citizens to win a majority.

ideaBank.idea: Treating voting as a civic duty comparable to jury service strengthens democratic legitimacy.
ideaBank.develop: High participation gives elected parliaments a clear mandate to enact long-term reforms on healthcare or infrastructure.

ideaBank.idea: Forcing citizens to the polls infringes upon the freedom to abstain as a form of protest.
ideaBank.develop: In a liberal democracy, the right to vote logically encompasses the right to withhold consent when no candidate represents one's principles.

ideaBank.idea: Reluctant voters may cast random or poorly informed ballots merely to avoid a penalty.
ideaBank.develop: Citizens who follow public affairs minimally might tick the top name on the paper, introducing arbitrary noise into close constituencies.

ideaBank.idea: Modest fines can still fall unfairly on citizens facing work shifts, illness, or administrative errors.
ideaBank.develop: Even small penalties burden casual workers or homeless residents unless registration is automatic and weekend or postal voting is widely available.

band8Model.text:
Declining voter turnout in many established democracies has renewed debate over whether casting a ballot should be treated as a legal obligation rather than a voluntary privilege. I largely agree that compulsory voting backed by modest fines strengthens democratic representation, provided citizens retain the option to submit a blank or formal abstention ballot.

The chief merit of mandatory participation lies in correcting the socio-economic skew inherent in voluntary elections. Where attendance is optional, older, wealthier, and more highly educated residents vote in far higher proportions than young adults or low-wage workers. Rational political parties respond by concentrating manifesto promises on the groups most likely to reach the polling station, leaving housing affordability, youth employment, and entry-level wages underprioritised. Requiring universal attendance shifts electoral incentives: candidates can no longer rely solely on inflaming partisan minorities and must instead formulate policies capable of attracting broad consensus across every demographic.

Opponents reasonably contend that compelling reluctant citizens to vote curtails personal liberty and increases the share of uninformed ballots. Forcing someone who distrusts every party to endorse a candidate would indeed compromise freedom of conscience. Yet this objection is readily addressed by distinguishing compulsory attendance from compulsory endorsement: if ballot papers include a recognised "none of the above" box and voting takes place on weekends with accessible postal options, citizens remain free to register principled dissent without facing unfair logistical hurdles. Moreover, empirical experience in countries with mandatory turnout indicates that knowing one must participate encourages citizens to pay closer attention to civic affairs rather than disengaging permanently.

In conclusion, legally mandatory voting—when paired with effortless access and an explicit abstention choice—reinforces civic responsibility and produces governments accountable to the entire public. Rather than eroding liberty, a light-touch obligation protects the equal voice on which democracy depends.

notes.noteVi: Lập trường đồng ý kèm cơ chế bảo vệ quyền tự do biểu đạt ("formal abstention ballot") ngay trong câu luận điểm.
Cụm danh từ học thuật súc tích ("socio-economic skew inherent in...") tóm gọn vấn đề bất bình đẳng cử tri.
Kết hợp collocation "formulate policies" và "broad consensus" tự nhiên, đối lập sắc bén với "inflaming partisan minorities".
Nhượng bộ thực chất bằng trạng từ nhấn mạnh "indeed" trước khi tách bạch khái niệm ở câu kế tiếp.
Phân biệt khái niệm rất sắc (bắt buộc đi bầu vs. bắt buộc chọn ứng viên), hóa giải trực tiếp lập luận phản đối về tự do.
Mệnh đề danh động từ lồng ghép ("knowing one must participate") làm chủ ngữ giúp câu mạch lạc, giàu học thuật.
Mệnh đề quan hệ trang trọng với giới từ đứng trước đại từ ("on which democracy depends") kết bài ấn tượng.

prompt: Many large corporations now rely on automated algorithms to screen job applications and shortlist candidates. Do the advantages of this practice outweigh the disadvantages?
partsToAddress: Examine the operational advantages of algorithmic screening for large employers
Analyse the ethical, fairness, and accuracy disadvantages for applicants and firms
Reach a clear judgement on whether the benefits outweigh the drawbacks

ideaBank.idea: Automated tools process thousands of applications within minutes, lowering recruitment overheads.
ideaBank.develop: When a multinational receives five thousand submissions for an entry-level vacancy, software filters basic qualification criteria far faster than human recruiters.

ideaBank.idea: Standardised scoring can reduce fatigue-driven inconsistency among human reviewers.
ideaBank.develop: Unlike overworked hiring panels whose attention wanes late in the afternoon, an algorithm applies identical threshold rules to the first and last curriculum vitae.

ideaBank.idea: Structured skill matching can widen pools beyond prestigious university names.
ideaBank.develop: When tuned to verify portfolio tasks and technical certifications, screening systems can surface capable self-taught applicants whom traditional recruiters might overlook.

ideaBank.idea: Models trained on historical hiring records frequently reproduce entrenched demographic bias.
ideaBank.develop: If past promotions favoured a particular gender or educational background, machine-learning filters inadvertently penalise qualified candidates from underrepresented groups.

ideaBank.idea: Keyword-based filtering rewards cynical optimisation rather than genuine capability.
ideaBank.develop: Candidates who stuff applications with software-friendly jargon advance ahead of skilled problem-solvers who describe unconventional career paths in plain language.

ideaBank.idea: Opaque rejection decisions erode applicant trust and expose firms to legal risk.
ideaBank.develop: Because proprietary models rarely explain why an individual was excluded, rejected jobseekers have no meaningful recourse to challenge flawed assessments.

band8Model.text:
Facing thousands of online applications for every advertised vacancy, major corporations increasingly deploy automated algorithms to filter curricula vitae and rank prospective hires. Although algorithmic recruitment delivers undeniable gains in speed and administrative efficiency, I believe its disadvantages currently outweigh its advantages whenever opaque systems operate without rigorous human oversight.

The operational appeal of automated screening is easy to appreciate. Manually reviewing massive applicant pools is labour-intensive, costly, and vulnerable to recruiter fatigue, which often causes strong submissions read late in the day to be skimmed superficially. Well-designed software can verify mandatory credentials, schedule assessments, and apply uniform baseline criteria within seconds, freeing human-resources specialists to spend more time conducting substantive interviews. In principle, anonymised skill scoring can also curb conscious prejudice by concealing names, ages, and prestigious institutional labels during initial shortlisting.

In practice, however, algorithmic hiring introduces an inherent drawback that undermines both fairness and talent quality. Predictive models trained on historical employment records routinely inherit and scale past inequalities: if a firm's earlier senior hires came predominantly from one demographic group or narrow career trajectory, the system learns to penalise career breaks, non-traditional degrees, and underrepresented applicants. Equally troubling is the opacity of proprietary scoring tools, which pose serious ethical questions when rejected candidates receive no explanation and cannot contest factual errors. Furthermore, reliance on rigid keyword matching encourages cynical formatting tricks while filtering out adaptable thinkers whose experience does not fit narrow templates.

In conclusion, while automation can usefully assist with logistical sorting, handing decisive shortlisting authority to unaudited algorithms risks institutionalising bias and forfeiting genuine talent. Until independent audits and transparent appeal rights become standard within a binding regulatory framework, the drawbacks of algorithmic hiring outweigh its efficiency gains.

notes.noteVi: Trả lời trực tiếp câu hỏi "outweigh" ngay câu luận điểm với điều kiện cụ thể ("opaque systems ... without rigorous human oversight").
Mệnh đề quan hệ không xác định kết hợp cụm phân từ quá khứ rút gọn ("read late in the day") và bị động nguyên mẫu ("to be skimmed").
Tương phản khéo léo giữa "In principle" (cuối đoạn 2) và "In practice, however" (đầu đoạn 3), tạo liên kết xuyên đoạn xuất sắc.
Cụm động từ chính xác cho chủ đề AI ("inherit and scale past inequalities", "proprietary scoring tools").
Đảo ngữ với tính từ ("Equally troubling is...") kết hợp collocation "pose serious ethical questions" rất tự nhiên.
Diễn đạt sắc nét về hạn chế của lọc từ khóa ("cynical formatting tricks", "narrow templates").
Kết bài chốt lại phán quyết rõ ràng, nhất quán tuyệt đối với mở bài và toàn bộ phân tích ở thân bài.

prompt: An increasing number of organisations now allow office employees to work remotely on a permanent basis rather than commuting to a central workplace. Do the advantages of this shift outweigh the disadvantages?
partsToAddress: Analyse the personal, organisational, and urban advantages of permanent remote work
Examine drawbacks such as social isolation, weaker mentoring, and blurred boundaries
State a clear overall evaluation of whether benefits exceed drawbacks

ideaBank.idea: Eliminating daily commutes reclaims substantial time and lowers household living costs.
ideaBank.develop: Employees save up to two hours each weekday previously lost to congested trains or motorways, reducing travel bills and freeing energy for exercise and family life.

ideaBank.idea: Location-independent roles widen talent pools and revitalise regional towns.
ideaBank.develop: Firms can recruit specialists regardless of postcode, while workers no longer need to pay inflated metropolitan rents, channelling spending into smaller communities.

ideaBank.idea: Quieter home workspaces often boost individual focus on analytical tasks.
ideaBank.develop: Without the constant chatter of open-plan offices, staff writing code, reports, or financial models complete deep work more efficiently.

ideaBank.idea: Permanent remoteness can weaken informal mentoring and stall junior staff development.
ideaBank.develop: Recent graduates lose the chance to observe senior colleagues handle negotiations or ask quick clarifying questions across a desk, slowing professional growth.

ideaBank.idea: Prolonged solitary work risks eroding team cohesion and employee mental health.
ideaBank.develop: Employees living alone in small flats may experience chronic isolation and feel disconnected from organisational culture when every interaction becomes a scheduled video call.

ideaBank.idea: Working from home frequently blurs the boundary between paid hours and personal rest.
ideaBank.develop: Without a physical departure from an office, conscientious workers often answer evening messages, increasing fatigue and strain on domestic relationships.

band8Model.text:
Advances in cloud software and video conferencing have enabled many firms to replace mandatory office attendance with permanent remote contracts. While full-time home working presents genuine hurdles for team cohesion and junior mentoring, I consider that its overall advantages outweigh its disadvantages for both employees and wider society.

The most tangible gains stem from the abolition of the daily commute and the geographic freedom remote work unlocks. Reclaiming one to two hours every weekday lowers commuting expenses, relieves work-related stress, and gives parents and carers greater flexibility to balance domestic obligations with professional duties. For employers, removing postcode restrictions broadens recruitment beyond expensive capital cities while trimming commercial real-estate overheads. At a wider civic level, fewer peak-hour commuters ease pressure on strained transport networks and allow professionals to relocate to more affordable regional towns, dispersing economic activity beyond overcrowded metropolitan cores.

Nevertheless, permanent remoteness carries notable drawbacks that organisations cannot afford to ignore. Spontaneous collaboration—the brief corridor conversations that spark creative solutions—rarely translates seamlessly into scheduled video calls. Newly hired graduates feel this loss most acutely, as they miss the informal observation and rapid feedback through which workplace judgement is ordinarily absorbed. In addition, employees sharing cramped flats or living alone risk persistent loneliness and an "always-on" culture in which professional messages intrude well into the evening. Yet these liabilities are largely manageable through deliberate management practices: clear disconnection policies, dedicated home-office stipends, structured mentoring pairs, and quarterly in-person retreats can preserve cultural cohesion without restoring wasteful daily commutes.

In conclusion, permanent remote work does require more intentional leadership to safeguard collaboration and mental wellbeing. Provided companies invest in those human routines, its substantial gains in time, affordability, and labour-market inclusion clearly outweigh its limitations.

notes.noteVi: Nêu rõ lập trường đánh giá lợi ích lớn hơn bất lợi ngay mở bài, đồng thời báo trước hai mặt phân tích ở thân bài.
Mở rộng góc nhìn từ cá nhân, doanh nghiệp lên cấp độ đô thị với cụm phân từ kết quả ("dispersing economic activity...").
Giải thích trực quan khái niệm "spontaneous collaboration" bằng cụm đồng vị cụ thể và động từ "translates seamlessly into".
Cấu trúc "through which + bị động" diễn đạt chính xác cơ chế học hỏi phi chính thức nơi công sở.
Câu bản lề cân bằng lại nhược điểm bằng nhóm giải pháp thực tế, giữ mạch lập luận đồng nhất với kết luận "outweigh".
Bốn biện pháp quản trị cụ thể giúp lập luận không bị chung chung, chứng minh các bất lợi hoàn toàn có thể khắc phục.
Tổng kết bằng ba danh từ trừu tượng đắt giá ("affordability", "labour-market inclusion") đúng chuẩn văn phong học thuật.

prompt: Many universities are replacing traditional multi-year campus programmes with flexible, modular online degrees that students can complete at their own pace. Do the advantages of this trend outweigh the disadvantages?
partsToAddress: Discuss how modular online degrees expand access, affordability, and lifelong learning
Evaluate what is lost if traditional campus programmes are replaced outright
Deliver a balanced verdict on whether the advantages outweigh the disadvantages

ideaBank.idea: Self-paced modular degrees widen access to tertiary education for working adults and carers.
ideaBank.develop: Learners who cannot pause full-time employment or relocate to a university town can accumulate recognised credits incrementally as their schedule allows.

ideaBank.idea: Online delivery sharply reduces tuition, accommodation, and relocation expenses.
ideaBank.develop: By removing student-hall rents and commuting costs, digital degrees prevent many first-generation graduates from entering adulthood burdened by heavy debt.

ideaBank.idea: Stackable modules allow syllabuses to be updated quickly alongside shifting industries.
ideaBank.develop: Mid-career professionals can enrol in targeted data-ethics or clean-energy units without committing to an inflexible three-year residential timetable.

ideaBank.idea: Fully online study removes the face-to-face community that nurtures interpersonal skills.
ideaBank.develop: Late-night seminar debates, student societies, and shared studio projects teach persuasion, empathy, and teamwork far more richly than asynchronous discussion boards.

ideaBank.idea: Self-paced formats suffer from lower completion rates due to heavy demands on self-discipline.
ideaBank.develop: Without fixed lecture routines and visible peer momentum, students facing work stress or domestic disruption frequently defer modules indefinitely.

ideaBank.idea: Practical disciplines and rigorous assessment are difficult to replicate remotely.
ideaBank.develop: Chemistry laboratories, clinical placements, and supervised examinations cannot be fully digitised without risking diluted academic standards or undetected misconduct.

band8Model.text:
Higher education institutions are increasingly unbundling three-year campus degrees into flexible, modular online qualifications that learners can pace around work and family commitments. While digital modular courses offer valuable flexibility when offered alongside conventional study, I believe the disadvantages outweigh the advantages if universities replace residential campus programmes altogether.

The strengths of modular online degrees lie primarily in widening access to tertiary education. For mid-career adults seeking to retrain, parents with caregiving responsibilities, or residents of rural towns far from major campuses, studying one credit-bearing unit at a time removes formidable financial and geographical barriers. Eliminating relocation and accommodation costs also curbs graduate debt, while modular design allows institutions to refresh technical units rapidly so that curricula remain aligned with evolving workplace standards. As a complementary route for lifelong learning, this format is undeniably progressive.

Replacing traditional campus programmes wholesale, however, would forfeit essential dimensions of university education that screen-based modules cannot replicate. First, self-paced online pathways place an immense burden on individual self-discipline; without regular in-person seminars, structured cohorts, and immediate faculty check-ins, dropout rates tend to climb sharply, particularly among younger or less confident learners. Second, higher education is more than content transfer. Laboratory experimentation, clinical workshops, and spontaneous intellectual debate across diverse student societies cultivate interpersonal skills, critical challenge, and enduring professional networks. Finally, remote assessment remains vulnerable to identity fraud and automated essay generation, potentially eroding employer confidence in rigorous academic standards.

In conclusion, modular online degrees excel as an accessible supplement for working learners and specialist reskilling. Nonetheless, because wholesale replacement of campus study compromises completion rates, practical training, and intellectual community, the drawbacks of abandoning residential programmes outweigh the gains.

notes.noteVi: Bắt rất sát động từ "replacing" trong đề bài để đưa ra phán quyết tinh tế: hữu ích khi bổ sung, bất lợi vượt trội nếu thay thế hoàn toàn.
Động từ học thuật hiện đại "unbundling" diễn tả chính xác xu hướng chia nhỏ bằng cấp thành các học phần độc lập.
Cụm từ chuyên ngành giáo dục đại học ("credit-bearing unit", "formidable ... barriers", "graduate debt") chuẩn xác.
Chuyển đoạn chặt chẽ bằng "however" chen giữa và nhấn mạnh chữ "wholesale" khớp hoàn toàn với luận điểm mở bài.
Cụm giới từ điều kiện phủ định ("without...") liệt kê ba yếu tố song song dẫn tới hệ quả rõ ràng.
Câu đơn ngắn gọn tạo nhịp nhấn sắc sảo trước câu giải thích mở rộng về kỹ năng giao tiếp và môi trường học thuật.
Cụm phân từ hiện tại kết hợp trạng từ hedging ("potentially eroding...") tránh khẳng định cực đoan.

prompt: In response to urban population growth, many cities are constructing high-rise mixed-use neighbourhoods that combine apartments, offices, and shops within the same blocks. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this approach to urban planning?
partsToAddress: Explain the principal planning, environmental, and social advantages of high-rise mixed-use blocks
Identify the major liveability, infrastructure, and affordability disadvantages
Conclude with a concise synthesis of both sides

ideaBank.idea: Concentrating homes, workplaces, and shops curbs urban sprawl and preserves green belts.
ideaBank.develop: Building vertically on brownfield sites accommodates growing populations without paving over surrounding farmland and wildlife corridors.

ideaBank.idea: Mixed-use proximity shortens daily trips and supports walkable, low-carbon living.
ideaBank.develop: When groceries, clinics, and offices sit downstairs or one tram stop away, residents walk or cycle for routine errands rather than relying on private cars.

ideaBank.idea: Active ground-floor retail creates lively, safer streets throughout the day and evening.
ideaBank.develop: Unlike single-use office districts that empty after dusk, blended blocks maintain steady footfall and natural surveillance across varied hours.

ideaBank.idea: Dense vertical towers can strain local utilities, schools, and green space if under-planned.
ideaBank.develop: Adding thousands of residents to a compact footprint without expanding water mains, primary school places, and neighbourhood parks degrades everyday liveability.

ideaBank.idea: High-rise living often brings noise, limited daylight, and weaker suitability for larger families.
ideaBank.develop: Commercial deliveries, late-night eateries, and shaded courtyards can compromise sleep quality and leave young children with few safe outdoor play areas.

ideaBank.idea: New mixed-use towers carry high construction and service-charge costs that push up rents.
ideaBank.develop: Expensive lift maintenance, fire-safety systems, and prime land prices frequently turn vertical regeneration zones into enclaves unaffordable for modest earners.

band8Model.text:
As metropolitan populations expand, urban planners increasingly favour high-rise mixed-use developments that stack residential flats above offices, clinics, and ground-floor retail. This compact planning model delivers clear environmental and mobility benefits, yet it also poses tangible challenges for infrastructure capacity and everyday liveability.

The foremost advantage of high-rise mixed-use neighbourhoods is land efficiency. Accommodating thousands of residents vertically curbs urban sprawl, shielding surrounding agricultural land and natural habitats from low-density suburban expansion. Equally significant is the shift in daily travel habits: when workplaces, supermarkets, and childcare centres lie within walking distance of apartments, households depend far less on private cars, reducing both commuting time and per-capita carbon emissions. Meanwhile, blending commercial activity with residential life ensures that streets remain populated from morning until evening, fostering local enterprise and enhancing perceived public safety compared with sterile business districts that empty after office hours.

Nevertheless, intense vertical density carries distinct drawbacks whenever design and civic investment lag behind construction. Concentrating large numbers of households within a narrow footprint can rapidly strain existing water networks, sewage lines, primary schools, and public clinics unless councils upgrade infrastructure concurrently. At the building level, living directly above restaurants and delivery bays exposes residents to persistent street noise, odours, and reduced natural sunlight, while tall towers rarely provide the affordable multi-bedroom layouts or private outdoor play space that families with young children value. Furthermore, high engineering standards and recurring lift and facade maintenance fees often inflate rents and service charges, risking the displacement of lower-income communities.

In summary, high-rise mixed-use neighbourhoods offer a powerful blueprint for sustainable urbanisation by shortening journeys and containing sprawl. Their long-term success, however, hinges on pairing vertical housing density with acoustic design, generous pocket parks, upgraded public services, and mandatory affordable units.

notes.noteVi: Mở bài bám sát dạng đề "What are the advantages and disadvantages" bằng cách khái quát cân bằng hai mặt ưu - nhược.
Collocation chuẩn "curbs urban sprawl" kết hợp mệnh đề phân từ "shielding..." mô tả lợi ích môi trường sắc nét.
Tính từ giàu hình ảnh học thuật "sterile business districts" tạo đối lập sống động với khu phức hợp nhộn nhịp.
Mệnh đề điều kiện phủ định với "unless" và trạng từ học thuật "concurrently" nêu rõ điều kiện tránh quá tải hạ tầng.
Chuyển mạch phân tích mạch lạc từ cấp độ hạ tầng đô thị xuống cấp độ sinh hoạt trong tòa nhà ("At the building level").
Cấu trúc đối chiếu bằng "while" kết hợp mệnh đề quan hệ xác định chỉ rõ tác động lên nhóm gia đình có con nhỏ.
Kết bài tổng hợp cân bằng cả hai mặt và chỉ ra bốn điều kiện quy hoạch thiết yếu để mô hình vận hành bền vững.

prompt: Some cities are investing in vertical indoor farms that grow crops in stacked, climate-controlled layers inside urban buildings. Do the advantages of urban vertical farming outweigh the disadvantages?
partsToAddress: Examine the resource, climate-resilience, and supply-chain benefits of vertical indoor farms
Evaluate economic and ecological drawbacks, especially electricity use and crop limitations
Provide a nuanced judgement on whether the advantages outweigh the disadvantages

ideaBank.idea: Closed-loop hydroponic and aeroponic systems drastically conserve water and eliminate run-off.
ideaBank.develop: Recirculating nutrient mists use a small fraction of the water required by open-field irrigation while preventing chemical pesticides from leaching into rivers.

ideaBank.idea: Year-round indoor cultivation shields urban fresh-produce supply from extreme weather.
ideaBank.develop: Droughts, unseasonal frosts, and floods cannot wipe out harvests inside climate-regulated warehouses, stabilising local availability and prices for salads and herbs.

ideaBank.idea: Growing produce close to supermarkets trims refrigerated freight distances and food spoilage.
ideaBank.develop: Harvesting greens within the city cuts transit times from days to hours, preserving nutritional freshness and minimising post-harvest waste.

ideaBank.idea: Artificial LED lighting and climate control demand substantial electrical energy.
ideaBank.develop: Replacing free sunlight with continuous indoor lighting can actually generate a larger carbon footprint than field farming wherever local power grids still rely on fossil fuels.

ideaBank.idea: Vertical farms are economically viable for only a narrow range of fast-growing crops.
ideaBank.develop: Calorie-dense staples such as wheat, rice, maize, and potatoes require too much space and energy indoors, meaning urban towers cannot replace rural agriculture.

ideaBank.idea: High start-up capital and urban real-estate costs make indoor produce expensive.
ideaBank.develop: Expensive sensors, racking, and city warehouse leases push retail prices above conventional produce, restricting access primarily to affluent shoppers.

band8Model.text:
Faced with volatile weather and elongated food supply chains, several municipalities have supported vertical indoor farms that cultivate crops in stacked, climate-controlled towers. In my view, the advantages of urban vertical farming outweigh its disadvantages only when it is deployed selectively for high-value perishable greens powered by renewable energy, rather than treated as a wholesale substitute for conventional agriculture.

Within that focused niche, indoor farming yields impressive ecological and logistical gains. Closed-loop hydroponic systems recycle nutrient water continuously, conserving resources by consuming far less water than open-field irrigation and eliminating agricultural pesticide run-off into local rivers. Because temperature, humidity, and light cycles are regulated year-round, harvests remain insulated from droughts, hailstorms, and heatwaves, bolstering urban food security for delicate crops. Locating production inside repurposed urban warehouses also slashes refrigerated transport distances; leafy vegetables reach neighbourhood grocers within hours of harvest, improving nutritional freshness and minimising spoilage along the supply chain.

Outside that niche, however, severe economic and environmental constraints emerge. Substituting free natural sunlight with intensive artificial lighting and ventilation entails heavy energy consumption; unless electricity comes predominantly from low-carbon sources, the resulting emissions can easily exceed those of imported field-grown produce. Moreover, high capital costs for urban real estate, sensors, and automation keep unit prices elevated, often putting vertically farmed goods beyond the reach of modest-income households. Most fundamentally, vertical structures remain unsuited to calorie-rich staples such as rice, wheat, maize, and pulses, which form the backbone of global human nutrition.

In conclusion, vertical indoor farming is neither a silver bullet for world hunger nor a flawed novelty. When paired with clean electricity and confined to perishable urban greens, its resource and resilience advantages outweigh its limitations—provided policymakers continue investing primarily in sustainable rural farming for staple crops.

notes.noteVi: Đưa ra đánh giá "outweigh" có điều kiện cực kỳ thuyết phục, phân định rõ phạm vi cây trồng và nguồn điện.
Từ vựng nông nghiệp đô thị chính xác ("Closed-loop hydroponic systems", "agricultural pesticide run-off", "bolstering urban food security").
Câu ghép tinh tế dùng dấu chấm phẩy và cụm phân từ hiện tại kép ("improving ... and minimising ...") nối nhân quả mượt mà.
Cụm đối chiếu trực tiếp với "Within that focused niche" ở đầu thân bài 1, tạo bố cục song hành rõ rệt.
Mệnh đề điều kiện "unless" kết hợp đại từ thay thế "those of..." tránh lặp từ "emissions" chuẩn xác.
Chạm tới giới hạn cốt lõi nhất về an ninh lương thực (không trồng được cây lương thực thiết yếu giàu năng lượng).
Cấu trúc "neither ... nor ..." với cụm từ sắc thái cân bằng giúp kết bài đọng lại ấn tượng học thuật cao.

prompt: Consumer wearable devices capable of continuously tracking heart rate, sleep quality, and blood oxygen levels have become widely available. Do the advantages of continuous personal health monitoring outweigh the disadvantages?
partsToAddress: Analyse the preventive and behavioural benefits of consumer health wearables
Assess risks involving false alarms, health anxiety, and biometric data privacy
State a clear judgement on whether the benefits outweigh the drawbacks

ideaBank.idea: Continuous biometric tracking can detect silent irregularities before emergencies occur.
ideaBank.develop: Alerts for irregular heart rhythms or sudden nocturnal oxygen drops prompt users to seek clinical evaluation early, catching conditions that occasional annual check-ups miss.

ideaBank.idea: Immediate feedback helps individuals cultivate healthier daily exercise and sleep routines.
ideaBank.develop: Visualising step totals, resting heart trends, and sleep consistency motivates sedentary adults to sustain gradual lifestyle improvements over months.

ideaBank.idea: Longitudinal home readings enrich consultations and reduce unnecessary clinic visits.
ideaBank.develop: Sharing several weeks of baseline heart-rate logs gives doctors richer context than a single five-minute measurement taken under stressful surgery conditions.

ideaBank.idea: Constant self-tracking can trigger obsessive health anxiety and unnecessary medical tests.
ideaBank.develop: Minor sensor fluctuations or imperfect sleep scores may alarm healthy wearers into booking repeated appointments, adding strain to already stretched primary-care clinics.

ideaBank.idea: Commercial handling of intimate biometric records creates serious data-privacy hazards.
ideaBank.develop: Without strict legal safeguards, private technology firms could monetise sensitive physiological profiles or share them with insurers to adjust premiums unfairly.

ideaBank.idea: Consumer-grade sensors can produce inaccurate readings that foster a false sense of security.
ideaBank.develop: Users who rely on wrist-based readings instead of formal clinical screening might ignore genuine warning symptoms simply because a device displays normal metrics.

band8Model.text:
Smartwatches and biometric rings now enable ordinary citizens to monitor heart rhythms, sleep cycles, and blood oxygen levels throughout every day and night. Although constant self-tracking brings valid concerns over anxiety and data privacy, I believe the advantages of wearable health monitors outweigh their disadvantages when devices are backed by sensible privacy rules and clinical literacy.

The chief benefit of continuous monitoring lies in shifting healthcare towards earlier disease prevention and personal agency. Traditional medical check-ups capture only a brief snapshot once a year, frequently missing intermittent heart arrhythmias or subtle declines in sleep quality. By logging longitudinal trends passively, consumer wearables can flag persistent anomalies early enough for timely clinical intervention, potentially averting strokes or chronic deterioration. Beyond early detection, real-time behavioural feedback helps sedentary individuals cultivate healthier habits: seeing measurable drops in resting heart rate after weeks of brisk walking or earlier bedtimes reinforces motivation far more effectively than abstract medical advice.

Critics nonetheless identify genuine drawbacks that merit careful regulation. Consumer sensors are less accurate than hospital instruments, and benign fluctuations or false alerts can trigger acute health anxiety among otherwise well users, prompting unnecessary clinic appointments that add pressure on overstretched health services. Conversely, misplaced faith in normal wrist readings may lull symptomatic individuals into delaying proper diagnosis. Equally pressing is data privacy: intimate physiological logs collected by commercial manufacturers could be breached, sold to advertisers, or exploited by private insurers unless strict statutory protections restrict secondary use. Even so, these hazards stem primarily from weak governance and poor user guidance rather than flaws inherent in preventive monitoring itself.

In conclusion, wearable health monitors offer a practical bridge between everyday habits and proactive medicine. Provided lawmakers enforce stringent biometric privacy standards and clinicians educate patients on interpreting alerts calmly, their preventive benefits clearly outweigh their drawbacks.

notes.noteVi: Mở bài trả lời trực tiếp câu hỏi "outweigh" kèm hai điều kiện thực tế (quy định bảo mật và hiểu biết y tế).
Từ vựng y học chính xác nhưng tự nhiên ("intermittent heart arrhythmias", "longitudinal trends", "timely clinical intervention").
Cụm danh động từ dài làm chủ ngữ kết hợp so sánh hơn nhấn mạnh ("far more effectively than...") rõ ràng, mạch lạc.
Dùng "Conversely" đối chiếu sắc nét hai thái cực rủi ro: lo âu thái quá (câu trước) và chủ quan bỏ qua triệu chứng (câu sau).
Chuỗi bị động song song ba động từ ("breached, sold..., or exploited...") kèm mệnh đề điều kiện "unless".
Câu bản lề cuối thân bài 2 tách bạch lỗi quản trị với bản chất công nghệ, củng cố vững chắc lập trường lợi ích vượt trội.
Ẩn dụ học thuật chừng mực, sáng ý ("a practical bridge ... proactive medicine") khép bài tự nhiên không sáo rỗng.

prompt: Retailers in several cities have begun deploying small autonomous delivery robots that travel along public pavements to bring groceries and parcels to doorsteps. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?
partsToAddress: Assess the commercial, emissions, and convenience benefits of pavement delivery robots
Examine spatial, accessibility, safety, and labour drawbacks on public footpaths
Reach a well-reasoned conclusion on whether advantages outweigh disadvantages

ideaBank.idea: Electric pavement robots can replace short diesel van trips for small local deliveries.
ideaBank.develop: Substituting lightweight battery-powered units for half-empty delivery vans reduces local exhaust fumes, engine noise, and kerbside double-parking.

ideaBank.idea: Automated last-mile fulfilment lowers operating costs and eases courier shortages.
ideaBank.develop: Supermarkets and pharmacies can dispatch urgent medicines or groceries during evenings without depending solely on scarce gig-economy drivers.

ideaBank.idea: On-demand doorstep robots offer practical independence for housebound residents.
ideaBank.develop: Elderly citizens or people recovering from surgery can receive small daily food orders reliably at predictable times.

ideaBank.idea: Commercial robots encroach on narrow footpaths meant for pedestrians and disabled users.
ideaBank.develop: Wheelchair users, parents pushing prams, and visually impaired residents relying on guide dogs face unexpected obstacles and collision hazards on already crowded walkways.

ideaBank.idea: Private corporations effectively privatise public civic infrastructure without paying rent.
ideaBank.develop: Municipal taxpayers fund and maintain pavements for human mobility, yet large logistics firms capture commercial savings by crowding footpaths with fleets of machines.

ideaBank.idea: Widespread automation risks displacing accessible entry-level courier employment.
ideaBank.develop: Local delivery riders, many of whom rely on flexible hours to support families or studies, face declining earnings if automated fleets dominate short-distance drops.

band8Model.text:
Small wheeled delivery robots are an increasingly familiar sight on city footpaths, ferrying groceries and takeaway parcels directly to residential doorsteps. Although these electric units promise lower emissions and operating savings for retailers, I contend that on dense urban pavements their disadvantages currently outweigh their advantages.

Proponents advance a plausible environmental and logistical case. Short-distance parcel runs performed by diesel vans contribute disproportionately to street-level air pollution, traffic delays, and illegal kerbside parking. Replacing such trips with compact, battery-powered robots can curb local exhaust emissions and reduce operating costs for supermarkets and pharmacies struggling with courier shortages. For housebound older residents or parents with sick children, dependable doorstep delivery of small essentials also brings genuine everyday convenience without putting another heavy vehicle onto residential roads.

Yet shifting commercial freight onto public pavements solves one transport problem by creating a more acute spatial inequity. Footpaths in most established cities are already narrow and cluttered with street furniture; introducing fleets of knee-high autonomous machines poses a serious risk to wheelchair users, visually impaired pedestrians navigating with canes, and parents pushing prams, particularly at junctions or during peak commuting hours. Equally questionable is the governance principle at stake: pavements are publicly funded sanctuaries for human movement, and allowing private corporations to monopolise them for profit effectively transfers private logistics burdens onto ordinary walkers. Beyond accessibility, rapid deployment threatens entry-level courier livelihoods while inviting vandalism and stalled units that block crossings whenever sensors misread winter weather or uneven kerbs.

In conclusion, autonomous delivery robots may serve a modest role on wide suburban walkways or enclosed university campuses under stringent regulations. Across bustling urban pavements, however, compromising pedestrian safety and equitable access to public space represents too steep a price for faster parcel convenience.

notes.noteVi: Lập trường rõ ràng ngay mở bài, đồng thời xác định bối cảnh không gian cụ thể ("dense urban pavements").
Câu mở thân bài 1 ngắn gọn, khách quan giới thiệu nhóm lập luận ủng hộ trước khi phân tích sâu.
Thuật ngữ quy hoạch đô thị sắc bén ("commercial freight", "spatial inequity") tóm trọn mấu chốt vấn đề.
Liệt kê cụ thể các nhóm người đi bộ dễ tổn thương giúp lập luận an toàn trở nên sống động và thuyết phục.
Đảo ngữ kết hợp dấu hai chấm mở ra phân tích sâu về công bằng hạ tầng công - tư, vượt lên mức liệt kê thông thường.
Mệnh đề phân từ bổ sung kết hợp mệnh đề quan hệ và mệnh đề thời gian ("whenever...") mượt mà, giàu chi tiết thực tế.
Cụm diễn đạt kết bài tự nhiên và chuẩn Band 8 ("too steep a price for...") đánh giá trực diện cán cân lợi - hại.

prompt: In many countries, shops and restaurants are rapidly moving towards cashless payment systems using cards and mobile wallets. Do the advantages of a cashless retail economy outweigh the disadvantages?
partsToAddress: Explain the practical, security, and fiscal advantages of cashless retail transactions
Consider financial inclusion, privacy, and technical resilience disadvantages
Conclude clearly on whether the advantages outweigh the disadvantages

ideaBank.idea: Contactless payments speed up checkouts and lower cash-handling costs for retailers.
ideaBank.develop: Shops save staff hours previously spent counting tills, ordering change, and paying armoured couriers to transport banknotes to banks.

ideaBank.idea: Reducing physical cash on premises bolsters security and improves tax compliance.
ideaBank.develop: Cafes and corner stores holding minimal banknotes become less attractive targets for robbery, while electronic trails curb underreported cash income.

ideaBank.idea: Digital records help consumers track everyday spending automatically.
ideaBank.develop: Mobile banking applications categorise grocery and transport purchases instantly, making monthly household budgeting simpler than keeping paper receipts.

ideaBank.idea: Refusing banknotes restricts access for elderly, low-income, and unbanked citizens.
ideaBank.develop: People without smartphones, bank accounts, or digital confidence can be locked out of basic shops, pharmacies, and public car parks.

ideaBank.idea: Fully electronic commerce leaves daily trade vulnerable to power or network failures.
ideaBank.develop: A regional banking outage or severe storm disrupting internet lines can halt food and fuel purchases instantaneously when no physical currency backup exists.

ideaBank.idea: Universal digital payments heighten privacy concerns and expose merchants to card fees.
ideaBank.develop: Every minor purchase generates a permanent data trail accessible to payment processors, while small independent traders lose a slice of each sale to transaction charges.

band8Model.text:
Contactless bank cards and smartphone wallets have swiftly displaced banknotes across shops, cafes, and transport kiosks in many economies. On balance, I believe the advantages of a largely cashless retail sector outweigh its disadvantages, provided governments protect the legal right to pay in cash at essential services.

The move towards electronic payments delivers compelling efficiency gains for businesses, consumers, and public finances alike. At busy checkouts, tapping a card or phone clears queues rapidly and frees small shopkeepers from counting registers, storing safes, and paying security firms to bank physical takings. Holding negligible cash on the premises also bolsters security by deterring opportunistic till theft. For governments, verifiable digital records narrow the shadow economy, helping authorities collect due tax revenue without raising headline rates. Meanwhile, shoppers benefit from instant spending summaries inside banking applications, making household budgeting considerably more transparent than tracking loose coins and paper receipts.

Nevertheless, a headlong rush towards a completely cash-free society entails serious social and operational risks. Most pressing is financial exclusion: elderly citizens accustomed to physical money, migrants lacking formal bank accounts, and low-income earners who budget weekly in banknotes can find themselves turned away from ordinary grocers or buses. Beyond equity, complete dependence on electronic rails introduces systemic fragility; when telecom networks fail during storms or banking software suffers an outage, cashless tills freeze instantly. Equally valid are privacy concerns, as routine purchases create detailed behavioural logs held by private intermediaries that also levy processing fees on independent merchants.

In conclusion, digital retail payments offer undeniable gains in speed, safety, and fiscal transparency that outweigh their limitations for the majority of citizens. Even so, preserving cash acceptance for essential goods and capping merchant card fees remain vital to ensure convenience never comes at the cost of inclusion or resilience.

notes.noteVi: Lập trường cân bằng, rõ ràng: lợi ích vượt trội nhưng cần giữ quyền dùng tiền mặt cho dịch vụ thiết yếu.
Cấu trúc song song ba cụm danh động từ ("counting..., storing..., and paying...") giàu chi tiết thực tế và chuẩn xác.
Thuật ngữ kinh tế tài chính chính xác ("shadow economy", "due tax revenue", "headline rates").
Câu chủ đề thân bài 2 mở ra hai nhóm rủi ro (xã hội và vận hành) được triển khai lần lượt đúng trình tự trong đoạn.
Cụm từ học thuật hiện đại ("electronic rails", "systemic fragility", "cashless tills freeze") diễn tả rủi ro công nghệ sắc nét.
Kết hợp mệnh đề nguyên nhân, cụm phân từ bị động ("held by...") và mệnh đề quan hệ xác định trong một câu mạch lạc.
Kết bài cô đọng, gói gọn toàn bộ trục đánh đổi giữa tiện lợi, hòa nhập xã hội và khả năng chống chịu hệ thống.

prompt: Rising housing costs and longer life expectancy have led more urban families to live in multigenerational households, where grandparents, parents, and children share one home. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this living arrangement?
partsToAddress: Explore the financial, caregiving, and emotional advantages of multigenerational urban homes
Examine the spatial, privacy, and interpersonal disadvantages of shared family living
Summarise both sides clearly in a balanced conclusion

ideaBank.idea: Pooling incomes and household bills eases steep urban housing and utility costs.
ideaBank.develop: Sharing one mortgage or rent alongside heating and grocery expenses frees young adults to build savings while protecting retired grandparents from inflation.

ideaBank.idea: Mutual caregiving lowers childcare bills and alleviates elderly loneliness.
ideaBank.develop: Grandparents can help with school runs and after-school supervision while enjoying daily companionship and prompt practical support as they age.

ideaBank.idea: Daily contact across three generations strengthens family bonds and cultural continuity.
ideaBank.develop: Children naturally absorb family stories, home languages, and culinary traditions through everyday meals rather than occasional holiday visits.

ideaBank.idea: Typical city apartments are rarely spacious enough to give three generations adequate privacy.
ideaBank.develop: Sharing a single bathroom or living room creates friction over noise, study space, and differing daily timetables between teenagers and older relatives.

ideaBank.idea: Generational disagreements over parenting, finances, and domestic chores can generate tension.
ideaBank.develop: Grandparents and parents often hold contrasting views on discipline or screen time, while unpaid caregiving expectations can fall unevenly on adult daughters.

ideaBank.idea: Co-residence may limit young adults' career mobility and sense of personal independence.
ideaBank.develop: Feeling obliged to remain in the family home to assist ageing relatives can deter working-age adults from accepting promotions in other cities.

band8Model.text:
Steep metropolitan property prices and rising longevity have prompted a growing number of city households to bring grandparents, working parents, and children together under one roof. While multigenerational living offers substantial financial relief and mutual emotional support, it also introduces notable pressures on privacy, domestic harmony, and personal autonomy.

The most immediate benefits are economic and practical. Pooling incomes across two adult generations spreads housing costs, utility bills, and food expenditure far more efficiently than maintaining separate urban flats, enabling younger couples to save while shielding older relatives from rising living expenses. Equally valuable is the reciprocal network of care such homes foster. Retired grandparents often assist with school collections and home-cooked meals, reducing costly nursery fees for working parents; in return, older family members gain daily companionship that alleviates loneliness and ensures prompt help during minor illnesses. Children raised in these households also tend to develop stronger empathy and a richer connection to family language and traditions.

Yet sharing compact urban housing across three age groups entails undeniable friction. Most modern city flats were designed for nuclear families rather than extended households, leaving teenagers, remote-working parents, and early-rising elders competing for quiet rooms and shared bathrooms. Without clear boundaries, differing attitudes towards child-rearing, household spending, and domestic chores frequently spark quiet resentment. Moreover, informal caregiving duties rarely divide equally; adult women in particular often shoulder disproportionate responsibility for both young children and frail elders while holding paid jobs, eroding their overall wellbeing. Co-residence can likewise restrict career mobility when younger adults hesitate to relocate for stronger employment prospects.

In conclusion, urban multigenerational households combine meaningful economic resilience and intergenerational warmth with real constraints on space, privacy, and individual independence. Whether the arrangement flourishes ultimately depends on adaptable housing design and explicit agreements regarding finances, boundaries, and shared domestic responsibilities.

notes.noteVi: Mở bài bao quát đầy đủ hai mặt lợi và hại theo đúng yêu cầu dạng đề "What are the advantages and disadvantages".
Cụm từ "reciprocal network of care" (mạng lưới chăm sóc hai chiều) kết hợp đảo ngữ rất tự nhiên và giàu ý nghĩa.
Dùng "; in return," thể hiện chính xác quan hệ tương hỗ hai chiều giữa cha mẹ trẻ và ông bà.
Mệnh đề phân từ hệ quả ("leaving + O + V-ing") mô tả sống động xung đột không gian giữa ba thế hệ.
Collocation chuẩn "shoulder ... responsibility for" kết hợp "overall wellbeing" chỉ rõ khía cạnh bình đẳng giới trong gia đình.
Dùng "likewise" bổ sung gọn một hệ lụy dài hạn về nghề nghiệp mà không cần dùng các cụm liệt kê cứng nhắc.
Mệnh đề danh ngữ bắt đầu bằng "Whether..." làm chủ ngữ tạo câu kết sắc sảo và cân bằng.

band8Model.text:
Leading cultural institutions are investing heavily in high-resolution photography and three-dimensional scanning to publish collections online through free virtual tours. Despite valid worries about funding pressures and the sensory limits of screens, I consider that the advantages of digitising museum holdings decisively outweigh the disadvantages.

The most compelling benefit is widening access to shared cultural heritage. Historically, experiencing iconic artefacts required costly travel to major capitals, excluding citizens on modest incomes, rural pupils, and people with mobility impairments. Free online galleries erase those barriers while unlocking reserve collections: since large museums display only a small fraction of their holdings in public rooms, searchable digital catalogues open vast archives of manuscripts, textiles, and ceramics to global scholars and learners alike. Equally critical is preservation. Detailed digital scans create an enduring archival record that lets historians study fragile objects without repeated handling and provides a vital blueprint should fire, flood, or conflict ever damage the originals.

Critics rightly note that a backlit screen cannot reproduce the tactile texture, monumental scale, or quiet reverence of encountering an original sculpture in person. There is also a financial concern: digitisation demands sustained spending on specialist imaging and software, and some curators fear free portals might erode ticket income. Yet viewing virtual tours as a rival to physical attendance misreads visitor behaviour. Much as recorded music expands demand for live concerts, engaging digital exhibitions frequently spark curiosity that motivates in-person visits, membership, and international exhibition loans. Directing a modest share of cultural grants towards digitisation also helps institutions maintain online access without neglecting gallery conservation.

In conclusion, although virtual tours cannot substitute for the sensory richness of walking through a physical museum, they need not do so to prove valuable. By democratising education, promoting cultural understanding, and safeguarding heritage for future generations, museum digitisation yields benefits that far exceed its drawbacks.

notes.noteVi: Mở bài khẳng định lập trường mạnh mẽ ("decisively outweigh") đồng thời thừa nhận hai mối lo chính của phía phản đối.
Đưa ra khía cạnh chuyên sâu ít người nghĩ tới (kho lưu trữ hiện vật không trưng bày), làm lập luận sâu sắc chuẩn Band 8+.
Đảo ngữ điều kiện với "should..." đặt mượt mà ở cuối câu giúp câu văn trang trọng và linh hoạt.
Chuỗi cụm danh từ giàu sắc thái mỹ học ("tactile texture", "monumental scale", "quiet reverence") thể hiện vốn từ rất rộng.
Câu bản lề ngắn gọn đảo ngược lập luận lo ngại sụt giảm doanh thu vé, nối sang phép so sánh tương đồng ngay sau.
Cấu trúc so sánh tương đồng học thuật "Much as..., ..." cực kỳ tự nhiên và thuyết phục.
Chuỗi ba động từ học thuật mạnh kết hợp collocation ("promoting cultural understanding", "safeguarding heritage") khép bài ấn tượng.
